$comment: What this release of Kanon needs of an adopter (plan 0005 §5.4, §5.5), read at the release's tag. Built from the lanes by tests/unit/requirements.test.ts, which fails when this file and the lanes disagree; rebuild it with KANON_WRITE_REQUIREMENTS=1 npx vitest run tests/unit/requirements.test.ts. `kanon init` writes callers, the hook and the App identities from it; `kanon doctor` checks an installation against a release's copy. `identities` are the names a lane's `<NAME>_APP_ID` secret carries: a role of rulebook/agent-permissions.json today, an App of it once the lanes take the Apps' secrets. A lane's `turns` is its turn limit and Kanon's ceiling on raising it for one dispatched run (kanon#891), through the `max_turns` and `reason` dispatch inputs `kanon init` writes on its caller. `catalogue` is the lane catalogue, and `features` the fixed sets of lanes offered in place of a choice per lane (plan 0007 §2), both copied from docs/lanes.json.

agent-review.name: Review
agent-review.does: Reviews a pull request labelled `review:please` (or `agent:triage` / `agent:implement`) once CI finishes on its head, or one you dispatch it for, and approves it or requests changes.
needs: your CI at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, whose runs it reads
agent-review.cost: A model run per reviewed head.
agent-review.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 445 runner-minutes a day: about 5 per reviewed head, while a run on a head with no review label, or one already reviewed, stops in under a minute.
agent-review.when: Always, and first: its App's approval is what ends bootstrap (`K-ADOPT-6`).

agent-merge-reconcile.name: Merge reconcile
agent-merge-reconcile.does: After a reviewed pull request merges, files a follow-up issue for each review suggestion it didn't apply.
agent-merge-reconcile.cost: A model run per merged pull request the Reviewer reviewed, except one whose reviews are all the Reviewer's and whose latest verdict declares zero open items.
agent-merge-reconcile.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 77 runner-minutes a day: about 4 per model run, while a run its filter skips takes under a minute.
agent-merge-reconcile.when: When the Reviewer's suggestions that a merge left out should become issues rather than be lost.

agent-implement.name: Implement
agent-implement.does: Builds a feature or resolves a spec delta from an issue labelled `agent:implement`, and opens a pull request.
agent-implement.cost: A model run per labelled issue.
agent-implement.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 143 runner-minutes a day: about 10 per labelled issue, while a run for any other label skips and bills nothing.
agent-implement.when: When you want agents to write code from the issues you label, once the Reviewer runs green.

agent-implement-revise.name: Implement, revise
agent-implement-revise.does: Revises the Implementer's own pull request when the Reviewer requests changes, or when the Merger hands back an approved head whose checks failed.
agent-implement-revise.cost: A model run per change request, capped in rounds.
agent-implement-revise.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 66 runner-minutes a day: about 8 per round, while a review or label on any other pull request stops in under a minute.
agent-implement-revise.when: With implement: without it, a change request on the Implementer's pull request waits for a person.

agent-explore.name: Explore (the sweep)
agent-explore.does: Sweeps your running product with a sweep hook you write, and files what it finds.
agent-explore.cost: A model run daily, skipped on a commit the QA store already holds a green sweep of.
agent-explore.minutes: Not measured: Kanon has no sweep hook, so it doesn't call the lane; a run costs as long as your sweep hook and the model take, daily.
agent-explore.when: When you can write a sweep hook that exercises your product, such as a Playwright run.

agent-code-audit.name: Code audit
agent-code-audit.does: Reads your code and specs every few days, and files a bug only on an objective contradiction.
agent-code-audit.cost: A model run every three days.
agent-code-audit.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 2 runner-minutes a day: about 10 per audit, every three days.
agent-code-audit.when: When you want a periodic second reading of the code, guided by `## Code areas` in your stack document.

agent-explore-telemetry.name: Explore the telemetry
agent-explore-telemetry.does: Reads Kanon's hosted telemetry aggregate weekly, never a row, and files or drafts the anomalies it finds in Kanon's lanes: failures by lane, stage, error and Kanon version, and costs per lane and model.
needs: a registration with Kanon's telemetry store that sets `aggregate_invoker`, which Kanon's operator sets; the lane reads the aggregate with GitHub's OIDC token, so no role, secret or variable (docs/telemetry.md)
agent-explore-telemetry.cost: A model run weekly, skipped when the aggregate holds no cell and no signal.
agent-explore-telemetry.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 1 runner-minute a day: about 6 per weekly run.
agent-explore-telemetry.when: When your telemetry registration sets `aggregate_invoker`, so you can read the aggregate.

agent-deploy-diagnose.name: Deploy diagnose
agent-deploy-diagnose.does: Reads a failed run of the deploy lane, its failed jobs' logs and the release's diff, and comments its diagnosis on the issue the deploy lane filed for each environment that failed. It deploys, re-runs and dispatches nothing, holds no cloud credential and runs none of your code.
needs: the deploy lane, with the environments `docs/qa/adoption.md`'s `## Deploy` section declares; `kanon init` writes this lane's caller only beside the deploy caller
a deploy log can hold resource names and account details, which reach the model: your adoption record's `## Data` answer covers what may
agent-deploy-diagnose.cost: A model run per failed deploy run, skipped when the run filed no issue.
agent-deploy-diagnose.minutes: Not measured: Kanon's own repository deploys nothing and calls no deploy lane.
agent-deploy-diagnose.when: With the deploy lane, when you want a first reading of a failed deploy on its issue before a person looks.

agent-triage.name: Triage and fix
agent-triage.does: Reproduces a bug labelled `qa:needs-triage`, rates it, and proposes a fix as a pull request.
agent-triage.cost: A model run per labelled issue.
agent-triage.minutes: At Kanon's pace, under a runner-minute a day: a run for any label but `qa:needs-triage` skips and bills nothing, and Kanon labelled no issue for it while measured.
agent-triage.when: When you file bugs for the agents to fix, or with explore or the code audit, whose findings it triages.

agent-issue-backstop.name: Issue backstop
agent-issue-backstop.does: Gives an issue opened with no milestone a bucket milestone (`K-WORK-1`), and flags a reviewer follow-up filed with no severity or, at a gate severity, without `gate-candidate`.
needs: the two bucket milestones, which `kanon milestones` creates
agent-issue-backstop.cost: No model; a short job per opened issue.
agent-issue-backstop.minutes: Not measured yet: Kanon has called it only since 2026-10-20; it runs once per opened issue, with no model, for well under a minute.
agent-issue-backstop.when: With implement or triage, once the Author App is installed: an issue filed by hand or through an issue form otherwise stays bare, and drops out of every progress report (`K-WORK-1`).

agent-lead.name: Lead, brief
agent-lead.does: Turns a mandate you dispatch into a project brief, opened as a pull request.
needs: project briefs under `docs/projects/`, from the brief template (`K-PROJ-1`)
agent-lead.minutes: Not measured: Kanon dispatched no mandate while measured; it runs only when you dispatch it.
agent-lead.when: When you want agents to plan work that spans several issues.

agent-lead-revise.name: Lead, revise
agent-lead-revise.does: Revises the Lead's own brief pull request when the Reviewer requests changes.
agent-lead-revise.cost: A model run per change request, capped in rounds.
agent-lead-revise.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 26 runner-minutes a day, nearly all of it runs on pull requests that aren't the Lead's briefs, each stopping in under a minute.
agent-lead-revise.when: With the Lead's brief: without it, a change request on a brief waits for a person.

agent-lead-split.name: Lead, split
agent-lead-split.does: Proposes splitting a project issue too big for one Implementer run, as a pull request against its brief.
agent-lead-split.cost: A model run per labelled issue.
agent-lead-split.minutes: At Kanon's pace, under a runner-minute a day: a run for any other label skips and bills nothing, and Kanon labelled no issue for it while measured.
agent-lead-split.when: With the Lead's brief, so an issue too big for one run is split rather than stalled.

agent-lead-reconcile.name: Lead, reconcile
agent-lead-reconcile.does: Drives an approved brief to done: files its issues, labels them for the Implementer in order, and closes the project once its merges are deployed.
agent-lead-reconcile.cost: No model; a short job on each merge and an hourly heartbeat, and a short check when a review, revise or implement run completes.
agent-lead-reconcile.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 77 runner-minutes a day: about a minute per closed pull request or issue, and per hourly heartbeat.
agent-lead-reconcile.when: With the Lead's brief: it is what turns an approved brief into work.

agent-verify-acs.name: Verify acceptance criteria
agent-verify-acs.does: Runs the tests that cite a project's acceptance criteria, and has the Explorer file what fails.
agent-verify-acs.cost: A model run per project verified.
agent-verify-acs.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 1.6 runner-minutes a day: a run for any other label skips, and Kanon verified no project while measured.
agent-verify-acs.when: With the reconciler, which asks it to verify a project before closing it.

agent-overseer.name: Overseer (optional)
agent-overseer.does: Audits the pipeline weekly from its aggregate, including its cost trend where your repository sends telemetry, and files what you can act on as `pipeline-improvement` issues. Where your adoption record turns the capability watch on, it also audits when a Kanon upgrade moves the agent runtime past its capability ledger's watermark.
agent-overseer.cost: A model run weekly, plus, where the capability watch is on, one when a Kanon upgrade moves the agent runtime forward. Every other merged Kanon upgrade runs only a short gate job.
agent-overseer.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 17 runner-minutes a day: about 21 per audit, while a run its gate turns away takes a few minutes.
agent-overseer.when: Once you run the Implementer, the Lead or the Merger unattended: it audits what runs without you watching (a lane that stopped, fixes that game their tests, follow-ups that leak, configuration drift, the cost trend). With only the Reviewer, or lanes you trigger by hand, you see every run anyway, and its first audits say little until weeks of history exist.

agent-project-digest.name: Daily project digest
agent-project-digest.does: Posts each open project's progress to a chat channel daily, and files an issue for a lane caller that keeps failing.
agent-project-digest.cost: A model run daily, only where the digest is posted: without a notify hook and `KANON_CHAT_PROJECT_DIGEST` it runs the health job alone, with no model.
agent-project-digest.minutes: Not measured: Kanon's caller is new and had not run yet; it runs once a day.
agent-project-digest.when: With the reconciler, when you have a chat channel for the developers.

agent-weekly-digest.name: Weekly digest
agent-weekly-digest.does: Posts the week's burndown and deliveries in plain language to a chat channel, for a stakeholder outside the day-to-day work.
agent-weekly-digest.cost: A model run weekly, only where the digest is posted: with no notify hook or no `KANON_CHAT_WEEKLY_DIGEST`, the gate job runs alone, with no model.
agent-weekly-digest.minutes: Not measured: Kanon has no notify hook, so it doesn't call the lane; it runs once a week.
agent-weekly-digest.when: When the Stakeholder is not the Owner and follows the project from outside, through a chat channel.

agent-release-announce.name: Release announcement
agent-release-announce.does: Posts each published GitHub release, a stable release or a pre-release, to a chat channel: its tag, its name and its notes as Features, Fixes and Maintenance, with a link to it.
needs: GitHub releases, published by a person or an App (a release the workflow token publishes starts no run)
agent-release-announce.cost: No model; a short job per published release. Without a notify hook or `KANON_CHAT_RELEASE`, the gate job runs alone.
agent-release-announce.minutes: Not measured: Kanon doesn't call the lane yet; it runs once per published release.
agent-release-announce.when: When the repository publishes GitHub releases and a chat channel should hear of each one, whether or not it deploys them.

agent-merge.name: Merge
agent-merge.does: Merges, with no person, an Implementer pull request the Reviewer approved with every check green, inside the green zone (`K-MERGE-4`).
agent-merge.cost: No model; a short job per review, per CI run on the default branch, and hourly.
agent-merge.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 110 runner-minutes a day: about a minute per review, per CI run on the default branch and per hourly sweep.
agent-merge.when: Once you have merged the Implementer's approved pull requests by hand for a while, and trust the green zone.
agent-merge.mergeQueue: Through a merge queue, a merge doesn't start its sweep: the queue's push runs CI as `github-merge-queue[bot]`, which the lane's gate turns away, so it sweeps on a review and hourly (#79).

agent-rebase.name: Rebase (resolve a conflict)
agent-rebase.does: Resolves a merge conflict on an agent's pull request, so its CI and review can resume.
agent-rebase.cost: A model run per conflicting agent pull request, checked on each CI run and daily.
agent-rebase.minutes: At Kanon's pace, about 57 runner-minutes a day: about 8 per conflict it resolves, while the check on each CI run takes about a minute.
agent-rebase.when: With implement or triage, whose pull requests otherwise wait for a person when they conflict: a person's rebase takes one out of the Implementer's chain, so the revise lane refuses it.

agent-dispatch-sweep.name: Dispatch sweep
agent-dispatch-sweep.does: Re-dispatches, once a day, an implement or triage run that never happened, and reports what waits on a person.
agent-dispatch-sweep.cost: No model; a short job daily, and a short check when an implement or triage run completes.
agent-dispatch-sweep.minutes: Not measured: Kanon's caller is new and had not run yet; it runs once a day, with no model.
agent-dispatch-sweep.when: With implement or triage, so a label whose event never arrived still starts its run.

leftOut.agent-explore-telemetry: It needs a registration that sets `aggregate_invoker`, which only Kanon's operator sets after the collector's first run registers the repository (docs/telemetry.md), so nothing done at install makes it work.
leftOut.agent-deploy-diagnose: It diagnoses the deploy lane's failed runs, and the deploy lane is in no feature: it runs only where the adoption record declares environments, so you ask for this lane beside it.
leftOut.agent-release-announce: It announces GitHub releases, which not every repository publishes, and nothing at install says whether this one will: you ask for it under Customise, or by name with `--lanes`.

environments.description: The declared environments, in deploy order, separated by spaces, exactly as the adoption record's `## Deploy` list names them. The gate refuses any other list.

environment.description: The environment to deploy, as the adoption record's `## Deploy` list names it.

position.description: The environment's place in the declared list, from 1. The lane refuses a call whose environment isn't at this position.

build.description: The build to deploy: `deploy-release.yml`'s `build` output, as the caller's `needs.release.outputs.build`. The lane downloads the artifact it names, which must be this run's, and checks it against its digest.

catalogue.name: Deploy
catalogue.does: Deploys each published release of a green default-branch commit to the environments the adoption record's `## Deploy` section declares, in order, the last being production: a gate, a trust probe of each environment's cloud role, one build with no credential, and one job per environment that deploys that build with your deploy and smoke hooks and that environment's OIDC credential. Records a `deploy` row per environment and keeps one issue per environment for its failures.
needs: a `## Deploy` section in `docs/qa/adoption.md` listing your environments
a GitHub environment per declared environment, production with required reviewers, or the record's fallback marker
a cloud role per environment that trusts only that environment's OIDC subject, readable from outside the environment (a repository variable)
the Releaser, so a release starts the lane
to announce each deploy, a notify hook and `KANON_CHAT_DEPLOY`, which the caller `kanon init` writes maps into each environment's job
catalogue.cost: No model. The gate waits for the release commit's CI, up to the declared CI wait (90 minutes by default); each environment costs what your deploy command costs.
catalogue.minutes: Not measured: Kanon's own repository deploys nothing and calls no deploy lane.
catalogue.when: When the repository deploys a system from its releases. It is not one of the features: an adopter that declares no environment has no deploy lane.
